races.name: William Hill Extra Place Races Daily Handicap

runners_data.name: Northern Express
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with strong course and going record (13/15 runs on similar ground); his chance hinges entirely on getting a free lead, which is far from guaranteed in this 19-runner field, and his recent form reads 3-6355 suggesting he is not at his peak even when things go right.
runners_data.comment: Without a win but rated well clear of this 19-strong field on our figures, some 13 lb above his official mark, with two thirds among the finishes in his last five starts. Trip and going are both proven, and a 15-day turnaround keeps him fresh into this one.

runners_data.name: Pellitory
runners_data.note: David Tudhope's booking for David O'Meara is a positive angle, and this consistent York specialist has strong positional sense at 7f on good ground; recent form of 550-00 is uninspiring but the course record suggests he shows up well in these conditions.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and with three of those finishes outside the frame, but the figures rate him a big step up on his official mark and much sharper than that recent line suggests. Trip and going are both proven, leaving fitness after a 22-day gap the main question.

runners_data.name: Yanifer
runners_data.note: Veteran 8-year-old who has placed twice at this trip on good ground and carries Ethan Tindall's 5lb claim; the trainer has a modest recent strike rate (2/7, 14 days) and a long break of 27 days may need a run to find full rhythm.
runners_data.comment: His form peaked with a win midway through the sequence and a couple of seconds just before it, but he has since fallen away, unplaced last time after a ninth. Trip and going are both proven, and the figures still rate him above his official mark, though that recent form needs reversing.

runners_data.name: Croupier
runners_data.note: Won twice at this course and distance on comparable going and carries course form as a major asset; 57-day break is a concern for fitness sharpness, but Joel Parkinson and Sue Smith have placed him carefully and his best form profiles perfectly for this shape.
runners_data.comment: Rated the second-best of these on our figures, well clear of his official mark, on the back of a win earlier in the run and a second since. A 57-day absence and a below-par ninth last time are the concerns, but the underlying form makes him a big threat.

runners_data.name: Morte Point
runners_data.note: Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim is useful, and he won over this exact trip and course on good ground last time out — his natural instinct is to race close to the pace, but with so many prominent types in this field he is likely to be bustled further back than he would prefer, which makes his chance harder to assess straightforwardly.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out following a string of well-below-par efforts, and a rapid 7-day turnaround suggests the yard likes what they saw. Trip and going are both proven, though the figures peg him only in line with his official mark, with plenty of below-par form still in the book.

runners_data.name: Angel Hunter
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon runner who landed a win on Standard ground last year; his York form reads 6-6-6-7 over 7-8f on good going and he has struggled to replicate that win, with headgear and 21-day freshness not obviously changing the picture.
runners_data.comment: A modest recent sequence of sixths and a seventh sits above a win earlier in the campaign, with an eighth the oldest run in a mixed picture. Trip and going are proven, and the figures still edge him above his official mark, but consistency is the query.

runners_data.name: Goldmoyne
runners_data.note: Consistent front-and-prominent horse with back-to-back second-place finishes on good ground at this trip; Cieren Fallon takes over with a 6-day turnaround, and while his sharp fitness is a positive, he needs to secure a clean prominent position in a congested early pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win but with two seconds among his last six starts, and a rapid 6-day turnaround keeps him ticking over on a going and trip that are both proven. Rated only in line with his official mark, he looks more of a makeweight than a live threat here.

runners_data.name: Wild Nature
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's 4-year-old won over this course and trip on Standard and has placed three times on good going; genuine hold-up style suits a scenario where the pace is strong enough to pull him into the race, and 13 days since his last run feels ideal.
runners_data.comment: A win in the middle of a patchy sequence is the highlight, with a pair of ninths further back and an unplaced run last time, and today's distance alone is proven. Rated only in line with his official mark and towards the bottom of these figures, he needs a lot to find.

runners_data.name: Milford
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho runner who holds up and has placed four times on good ground but primarily at 6f, and stretching to 7f at York on Good to Firm raises a question about whether he can sustain the finish after travelling for longer.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but rated a big step up on his official mark, with a fourth the best of a modest sequence otherwise made up of two unplaced efforts. Trip and going are both proven, and the figures make him one to respect despite the workmanlike form.

runners_data.name: Lir Speciale
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's 7-year-old has four places from his last five runs including two seconds and runs over a trip and surface that suits; positional racer who should get a decent berth behind the lead group if the prominent pack ahead tightens.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time and placed a couple of times before that, he is up to 6th of 19 on our figures, well above his official mark and helped by a strong speed figure. Trip and going are proven, though he remains without a win in his last five and the yard is cold (1/22).

runners_data.name: Our Havana
runners_data.note: Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim is a tactical angle, and this horse won over this exact trip on good ground most recently; rated 86 and coming off a win, he will be prominent and his 7f good-ground profile is directly applicable.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out to break a run of three finishes outside the frame, and the figures now have him a touch above his official mark. Trip and going are both proven, though a 28-day gap since that success adds a note of caution.

runners_data.name: Tilted Kilt
runners_data.note: Hector Crouch partners this hold-up type who won over 8f on Standard ground and placed on good going at that trip; the 7f drop from his preferred distance and his preference for more ground in front of him may make it hard to land a blow from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: A win three starts back is sandwiched between below-par efforts, and the form has cooled to an unplaced run last time. Trip and going are both proven, but the figures rate him near the bottom of this field and only fractionally below his official mark.

runners_data.name: Lord Roxby
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's 4-year-old has strong sprint form and prefers to race up with the pace on good ground — genuinely prominent in style — but the density of pace-seeking rivals in this 19-runner field means he is realistically being pushed back from where he wants to be, and his last two runs on 6f may mean 7f is stretching him.
runners_data.comment: A win in his recent form has been followed by finishes of fourth and fifth, a fair level of consistency for this grade, and a rapid 9-day turnaround keeps him fresh. Trip and going are both proven, with the figures rating him a step above his official mark.

runners_data.name: Rare Change
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes runner who won at 7f on soft and has headgear noted; drops back to a hold-up role here with genuinely competitive recent form (1-3-9 last three), though his best going profile leans slightly softer than today's Good to Firm.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out but that followed two unplaced efforts and a run of finishes that dips as low as ninth, so the strike was more the exception than the rule. Trip and going are both proven, and the figures leave him only just above his official mark.

runners_data.name: Andesite
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's 4-year-old with Kevin Stott up has placed at 7-8f on good ground in four of his last five runs, including back-to-back seconds; a genuine hold-up horse with consistent late-finishing form who needs the pace to be strong enough to reel in the prominent types.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts but with two seconds among the recent finishes and nothing worse than a seventh, this is a genuinely progressive-reading profile. Trip and going are both proven, a 13-day turnaround keeps him ticking over, and the figures rate him well above his official mark.

runners_data.name: King Casper
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer runner returning after 287 days off — a significant fitness concern — and while his two-year-old form on good going showed promise, the long layoff and the step into a 19-runner competitive handicap make his chance highly speculative.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts and out of the game for 287 days, so fitness is the obvious question, though a fourth and a fifth earlier in the sequence show he has ability. Trip and going are both proven, and the figures still edge him above his official mark.

runners_data.name: Son
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby has an outstanding 14-day strike rate (16/98) and David Allan knows this horse well; a natural hold-up runner who has placed three times from his last five on good ground at 7f, but the redistribution note reflects that more closers than ideal are sharing the same rear-of-field real estate today.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts but with two seconds among the finishes and a fair third earlier on, the underlying form is respectable. Trip and going are both proven, and the figures rate him well clear of his official mark, though a 10-day turnaround is swift.

runners_data.name: Canvas
runners_data.note: Scott Dixon's 4-year-old won over 8f on good ground and placed at that trip too, but is another genuine hold-up type squeezed into a midfield mapping by the volume of closers in this field; dropping back from 8f to 7f on faster ground is not obviously in his favour.
runners_data.comment: Rated bottom of this field on our figures despite a win at the start of this run, with only midfield-and-worse finishes since, unplaced last time. Trip and going are both proven, though there is little recent evidence beyond that early success to suggest a bounce-back here.

runners_data.name: Quest For Fun
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's veteran 8-year-old is a natural front-seeker with a tongue-tie, but the combination of a 48-day break, competitive rating at OR 77, and the reality that he cannot get to his preferred position in this field are all working against him today.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts and with more below-par efforts than good ones, including a ninth and an unplaced run in there, but a third last time was a step forward. Trip and going are both proven, and the figures rate him usefully above his official mark.

races.paceDynamic: Northern Express is the one confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field on Good to Firm ground at York, and with Paul Mulrennan likely to slot him into his natural lead role, he sets what should be a sustainable, measured gallop rather than a breakneck pace. The problem is that Pellitory, Yanifer, Croupier, Goldmoyne, Angel Hunter, Lir Speciale and Our Havana all want to race prominently, meaning there is a significant volume of pace pressing behind the leader and the race is unlikely to crawl. This field carries more front-running and prominent energy than can be accommodated up front — Morte Point, Lord Roxby and Quest For Fun are genuine pace-seeking types but are most likely to be shuffled back from their natural position by the sheer weight of horses seeking the same ground, with Pellitory, Croupier and Goldmoyne best-placed to actually secure prominent berths. The net effect is a race run at a genuine, honest gallop that will not wait for closers but will also not implode into a sprint finish — the shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently or in the first half of the field and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs, rather than pure hold-up horses who will need a strong pace collapse that this race is unlikely to provide.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Northern Express leads at a genuine but not punishing tempo and the prominent pack race in an organised fashion behind him, the race is run to suit horses who travel well in the first six and finish strongly.
scenarios.body: The Good to Firm surface at York rewards a fluid, prominent-racing type who never has to change gear abruptly, and a controlled honest gallop means the front rank is not decimated early; horses like Croupier, Our Havana and Goldmoyne, who combine positional sense with proven form on this surface, are best equipped to sustain to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Storm
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack press Northern Express harder than expected early, burning each other off, creating a strong pace that leaves the front rank vulnerable in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With the field strung out and the principals tiring, the genuine hold-up horses get the strong pace they need and can pick up sharply on the Good to Firm ground; Andesite and Wild Nature, who have demonstrated late-finishing form at this trip, are best suited to this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Controls, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Northern Express is allowed to dictate at a completely uncontested, comfortable tempo and the prominent pack fail to apply any meaningful pressure through the early stages.
scenarios.body: A lone front-runner who controls every yard on a flat, fair track with no natural check points can be exceptionally hard to catch; Northern Express has significant course and going experience (13 of 15 runs on similar ground) and though his recent form has been modest, an uncontested lead completely changes his profile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge, Value Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops with a bunched midfield and multiple prominent types crowd each other, creating a chaotic pace picture that benefits horses with the tactical versatility to find a run late.
scenarios.body: Horses mapped to midfield due to redistribution — including Morte Point and Lord Roxby — may actually find themselves in a better position than predicted if the pace scramble forces them into an advantageous spot; their natural speed means they can pick up quickly on Good to Firm if gaps appear.

watchPoints.text: Croupier and Our Havana are both proven prominent horses with wins at this course and trip on comparable going — if both secure clean prominent positions and the race runs at a genuine but not excessive gallop, they represent the two most dangerous winning profiles in this field.

The sheer volume of prominent-seeking horses (Northern Express, Pellitory, Yanifer, Croupier, Goldmoyne, Angel Hunter, Lir Speciale, Our Havana) means the opening quarter-mile could see a fierce positional scramble — watch for early crowding on the outside that could compromise the chances of horses drawn wide who need to find cover.

King Casper returns after 287 days off and is effectively unknown on fitness — any strong market move in the pre-race period warrants attention as it may suggest the stable has seen enough at home, but fade him on form alone until proven.

Morte Point, Lord Roxby and Quest For Fun are all natural pace types who are likely to end up racing out of their preferred position — if any of them do manage to secure prominent ground against the odds, their presence could meaningfully increase the early tempo beyond what Northern Express alone would create.

Rare Change and Andesite are the two hold-up horses with the most consistent recent placing form on similar going — in the event of a true strong-pace scenario developing, they are the closers best equipped to benefit rather than the horses redistributed to midfield from other natural styles.

races.name: William Hill Summer Stakes (Fillies' & Mares' Group 3)

runners_data.name: Celandine
runners_data.note: Consistent in similar conditions (11/13 sim-going runners beaten on good) but her natural front-runner's style is likely to be compromised by the traffic ahead of her; Charles Bishop will need luck in running from a position she would not ordinarily choose.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, though second earlier in that sequence points to some ability, and the six-furlong trip and good-to-firm ground are both proven. A below-par eighth last time and a 41-day gap temper things, but she is rated above her official mark.

runners_data.name: First Instinct
runners_data.note: Predominantly a 5f horse stepping up to 6f again after a career win over that trip in softer ground; William Haggas sends her here with a modest recent strike rate, and she will need to prove the extra furlong on fast York ground is within her compass.
runners_data.comment: Rated well clear of most in this field on our figures, with a strong speed figure to match, and both trip and ground are proven. The worry is recent shape — a ninth and unplaced runs of late, some way below the level shown when winning earlier in the campaign.

runners_data.name: Flora Of Bermuda
runners_data.note: Won over this exact course, distance and going profile last time out and boasts the strongest 6f York form in the field; James Doyle partners a filly who should be able to slot into a genuine prominent position without the scramble affecting her, and five of her last eight runs have been over this exact trip.
runners_data.comment: Rated the best of these on our figures, and the form backs it up — a win two starts back followed by a below-par effort last time that looks forgivable. Trip and going are both proven, and a 20-day break should have her ready to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Fluorescence
runners_data.note: Primarily a 5f specialist who has won twice at that distance; the drop back from her recent runs and the step up to 6f on good-to-firm ground raises doubts, and she is the type of front-runner who will find space squeezed by the stronger prominent rivals here.
runners_data.comment: Rated among the tail of this field, and a mixed sequence including an unseated-rider run does little to inspire confidence. In credit, she has won before at today's trip and going, both of which are confirmed suitable, and a fourth last time was at least workmanlike.

runners_data.name: Hold A Dream
runners_data.note: 69 days off the track for Clive Cox, and while she has strong course form at 6f on good ground her trainer's 14-day strike rate of 2/8 is modest; she races prominently and will likely find herself pushed further back than she'd like in this congested shape.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in her last five starts but has flashed ability, notably when second three starts back, and both trip and going are proven. A 69-day absence is the obvious concern, though our figures still nudge her ahead of her official mark.

runners_data.name: Kinswoman
runners_data.note: Effective at 5f on soft ground with three wins at that trip, but stepping up to 6f on Good to Firm is a different challenge; William Haggas doubles up in the race and she looks the second string, likely to find this surface and distance catching her out.
runners_data.comment: Rated near the foot of the field despite a win earlier in this run, with the finishes since — second, sixth, and a below-par ninth last time — trending the wrong way. Trip and going are both proven, but the figures suggest she needs a lot to find in this company.

runners_data.name: America Queen
runners_data.note: The only 3-year-old in this field with a 5/5 record on similar going and a course win over 6f; Richard Hughes' filly will be competitive from a prominent pitch, and at OR 107 she arrives with strong credentials for this exact test.
runners_data.comment: Rated the second-best in the field on our figures, with a run of places (second, fourth, second) either side of a win underpinning the claim. A below-par eighth last time is the outlier, but trip, going and a 20-day break are all in her favour.

runners_data.name: Catching The Moon
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in two wins over 5-6f but off 83 days, and Richard & Patrick Fahey's filly is fundamentally a pace-pressing type who has been redistributed toward the rear simply because of traffic; she is not a natural closer and her chance is most dependent on getting a cleaner passage than the mapping suggests.
runners_data.comment: Won two of her last four starts and was runner-up in the other, so the ability is clear, but a below-par unplaced effort last time and an 83-day layoff both raise questions. Trip and ground are proven, and the figures still just about back her.

runners_data.name: Figjam
runners_data.note: Winless in her last four on good ground and her best form has come over 6-7f on soft; Katie Scott's trainer strike rate of 0/15 over 14 days is a clear flag, and she is unlikely to improve from a midfield berth she does not naturally want.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last five and rated near the foot of this field, though she has hit the frame, including a second earlier in the sequence. Trip and going are proven and a quick 16-day turnaround keeps her ticking over, but she needs more to trouble these.

runners_data.name: Fitzella
runners_data.note: Five straight runs on good going with a best of 2nd over 7f, consistent without winning; Hugo Palmer's filly wants to race prominently but will find it difficult to assert in this congested pace picture, and her lack of a win at this level leaves her needing a career-best effort.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but a fair second earlier in that sequence, and a run of 5-6-5-5 either side shows a want of consistency rather than a lack of ability. Trip and going are both proven, and the figures rate her comfortably above her official mark.

runners_data.name: Royal Fixation
runners_data.note: Two wins over this exact 6f course on good ground and OR 111 at the head of the weights for Karl Burke; Sam James takes over in the saddle on a filly whose recent tailed-off run (7th at 55 days) is the only doubt, and she profiles as one of the very few genuine prominent types who can secure the right position.
runners_data.comment: Won two of her last five starts and was runner-up in another, a solid sequence undone only by a below-par seventh last time. Trip and going are both proven, but a 55-day gap and a figure below her official mark add a note of caution.

runners_data.name: Soul Love
runners_data.note: Three wins in her last four, all at 6f, with two on standard/fibresand and one on good; she is naturally a pace-pressing horse placed at the rear by field dynamics rather than by choice, and Pierre-Louis Jamin will need a trouble-free run to unlock her best from an unnatural starting position.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in her last four starts, including last time out, look eye-catching on paper, but our figures rate her near the bottom of this field, some way below her official mark. Today's distance is proven, though a 69-day gap adds to the question marks.

runners_data.name: Spicy Marg
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who sets the entire tactical framework for this race; Hector Crouch can dictate on her own terms, but her recent form reads 4-1-8-3-2 and she steps up from a 5f win last time, so sustaining the lead over 6f against high-class rivals is not guaranteed despite the tactical advantage she holds.
runners_data.comment: A strong hand among the dangers. She was runner-up last time out and lands a win earlier in a largely progressive sequence, proven over today's trip and going. A below-par run in the middle of the form is the one blip, but the figures single her out.

races.paceDynamic: Spicy Marg is the confirmed sole front-runner in this 13-runner Group 3, and on Good to Firm ground at York she should be able to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop without any genuine pressure from a true pace rival. The field is packed with prominent-racing types — Fitzella, Celandine, Hold A Dream, Kinswoman, Fluorescence, Figjam and Catching The Moon all want to race close to the pace but cannot all occupy those positions simultaneously, meaning several will be shuffled wider or further back than ideal. The result is likely to be a compact, bunched-up group chasing Spicy Marg in the early stages, with the real scrimmaging happening for the two or three spots directly behind her rather than at the front itself. This race shape — a single uncontested leader setting an honest but unfrantic tempo on fast ground over six furlongs — strongly favours horses who can track close to the pace in the first two positions and produce a sustained finish, giving the advantage to the genuine prominent racers who can actually secure that spot (Flora Of Bermuda, America Queen, Royal Fixation) over those artificially mapped further back. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can realistically get their position; of those, Flora Of Bermuda, America Queen and Royal Fixation are best placed to secure the coveted positions just behind Spicy Marg.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Spicy Marg Leads Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Spicy Marg breaks smartly and sets a fair but unforced tempo, with no rival able to pressure her early.
scenarios.body: She controls the fractions on Good to Firm York ground and the race becomes a sustained test of finishing speed from the front two or three positions, exactly the shape her profile suits; horses who travel prominently just behind her without burning energy scrapping for position are best armed to challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage, Strong Finisher Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion of prominent types causes a messy early shuffle and the pace becomes genuinely hot through the first two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The pressure created by multiple horses wanting the same slots forces a faster tempo than Spicy Marg intended, and the race begins to suit a runner who settles just off the speed and finishes powerfully; the Good to Firm surface keeps the race honest rather than letting any hold-up type coast home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Type Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and the front group tie each other up in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires horses mapped to the rear to be true closers, but Catching The Moon and Soul Love are naturally prominent types redistributed to hold-up roles, meaning their finishing kick from the back is not their genuine profile; only if pace is truly fierce does this shape have any credibility, and even then these are not natural beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Lone Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent traffic behind Spicy Marg checks each other's progress and she steals an unassailable lead turning for home.
scenarios.body: With a single front-runner and a bunched pursuit group there is always a chance the scrimmaging behind her is fatal for those involved and Spicy Marg simply extends; however her recent form and trainer's 14-day strike rate of 2/24 tempers enthusiasm for this outcome as a primary shape.

watchPoints.text: Flora Of Bermuda and America Queen are the two prominent types best placed to track Spicy Marg — watch whether either is forced to race wider than ideal at the break, which would compromise their chance of getting the perfect ground-saving position.

The redistribution of Catching The Moon and Soul Love to the rear is artificial — if either jockey pushes forward to reclaim their natural prominent pitch in the first furlong, it could accelerate the tempo sharply and change the entire shape of the race.

Royal Fixation's last run was a tailed-off 7th after 55 days off; watch the paddock closely for signs she is fully tuned, as her form profile is strong but that run raises a fitness question Sam James will need to answer quickly from the gate.

Hold A Dream returns after 69 days for Clive Cox — one of the longer layoffs in the field — and prominent-style runners returning from a break at York's flat 6f can be slow to find their stride; watch whether Finley Marsh elects to push up early or settle for a quieter position.

With 10 of 13 runners wanting prominent positions, watch the first two furlongs for crowding on the stands-rail side — any runner forced wide early at York over 6f will cover extra ground that is hard to recover on fast ground at this level.

races.name: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Laura Barry Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: Luzon Heights
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter here; William Knight's 3yo has won/placed on good-to-firm ground and sets the tactical tempo for the whole race, though a style-fit flag suggests its chance is best assessed as a pace influence rather than a standout winner.
runners_data.comment: Frame finisher in four of his last five starts without a win in that spell, most recently a second. Fit from a run 14 days ago and with form over today's trip and going, he tops our figures and looks the chief danger to the field.

runners_data.name: Get Outta Here
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's 3yo has a win and three places from five runs on this trip and going combination, making it a strong profile fit; Hector Crouch takes over and the horse's natural prominent style slots in cleanly behind the leader.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and a strong threat, with a win earlier in his last five for solid evidence of ability. Fit after a run 21 days ago and proven over today's trip and going, he rates prominently on our figures, though a patchier spell deeper in the form is the one query.

runners_data.name: Zarvali
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's 3yo is 7-from-7 in similar going and steps back up to a mile after a third at 7f — the switch back in trip is interesting, and Kevin Stott's low-key approach from a prominent berth could prove very effective here.
runners_data.comment: A win in the middle of his last five starts, with a runner-up effort alongside it and a third last time, points to solid form. Fit after a run 24 days ago and with form over today's distance, he is our selection on that shape even without topping the figures.

runners_data.name: Bee Farmer
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's charge has shown one placed effort from three starts and can track the pace from a prominent position, though its form string is short and the lack of a win in three starts asks a question of its finishing resolve.
runners_data.comment: Only a runner-up effort from three recent starts stands out, with modest finishes either side of it. He has form over today's trip and going but rates down the field on our figures, leaving little in reserve against this company.

runners_data.name: Spectical
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 3yo is equipped with a hood and has an unknown running style, making it genuinely hard to place tactically; James Doyle is a significant booking and the horse's best form came on similar going, though no wins in three starts tempers expectation.
runners_data.comment: A trio of modest finishes without a win puts a workmanlike look on his recent form. Fit from a run 22 days ago and with form over today's distance, he sits mid-table on our figures and needs to find more to threaten the principals.

runners_data.name: Hambelton
runners_data.note: David Marnane's 3yo won on good ground at a mile and is a genuinely prominent-racing type, but with the front slots already filled by Luzon Heights, Get Outta Here, and Zarvali, it is likely to find itself racing further back than suits — the style-fit discount applies.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out to end a modest run of finishes on a high note. Fit after a run 26 days ago and with form over today's distance, he sits mid-table on our figures and will hope that latest success marks an upturn.

runners_data.name: Illy's Roo
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason rides the Gemma Tutty-trained hold-up horse, who wears a hood and has struggled to reproduce a one-time placed effort in recent outings; seven consecutive seventh-place finishes on good ground are a significant concern over this track.
runners_data.comment: A win at the start of this six-run sequence and a third soon after show real ability, and our figures put him well above his official mark. Fresh from 35 days off and proven over today's trip and going, he poses a strong threat. The risk is a run of moderate efforts since, including three sevenths.

runners_data.name: Forest Phoenix
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 3yo has a finish-fading flag attached — a notable red light for a hold-up runner at York over a mile where you need to be travelling into the straight; the step up from 5-6f in form makes the trip itself a question mark.
runners_data.comment: A win the run before last was undone by a well-beaten effort next time, unplaced last time out. He has form over today's trip and going but rates bottom of this field on our figures despite a fair official mark, leaving plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Napolian
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope partners David O'Meara's 3yo, who is naturally prominent-minded and won on good ground over a mile; displaced into midfield by the volume of pace in this field, the style-fit discount is real and its best chance depends on getting closer than the race shape allows.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, a fair return after a mid-sequence dip. Fit after a run 15 days ago and with form over today's trip and going, he rates comfortably above his official mark on our figures and can build on that latest success.

runners_data.name: Milford Grange
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby's hold-up 3yo has a string of placed efforts but exclusively on soft ground — its sole good-ground run produced a third at 6f, and stepping to a mile on faster ground here is a clear concern.
runners_data.comment: Three seconds and a third among his last five starts show admirable consistency without a win to show for it. Fit from a run 20 days ago and with form over today's distance, he sits mid-table on our figures and remains capable of another honest showing.

runners_data.name: Only Dream Big
runners_data.note: Warren Fentiman claims 3lb for Tim Easterby; the horse has won twice recently from hold-up tactics and is tagged as a true hold-up type mapped to midfield — two recent wins suggest form, but the style redistribution means it may not get the strong pace it needs to deliver those finishing runs.
runners_data.comment: Won her last two starts before a flatter spell of finishes further back, an inconsistent profile at face value. She has form over today's trip and going but rates down the field on our figures, needing to rediscover that early form to feature.

races.paceDynamic: Luzon Heights is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead among the other confirmed pace-holders, is set to bowl along at a sustainable, controlled tempo on good-to-firm ground around York's flat mile. Get Outta Here, Zarvali, and Bee Farmer will track closely from the prominent positions, creating a compact early order, while Hambelton and Napolian — both natural prominent types — are likely to find themselves shuffled into a midfield berth against their instincts as the early slots fill up. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Luzon Heights is best placed to secure the lead, with Get Outta Here and Zarvali most likely to take the next positions, leaving Hambelton and Napolian racing further back than ideal. An uncontested, measured gallop through the first half of the race followed by a controlled acceleration from the two-pole strongly favours horses who can race prominently and sustain their effort — hold-up horses will face a stern test of whether the pace was truly honest enough to set them up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Strong Stayer
scenarios.trigger: If Luzon Heights dictates an unchallenged, even tempo and the race develops into a test of sustained galloping ability from two out.
scenarios.body: Luzon Heights rolls along without pressure, setting a metronomic pace that suits those who have tracked within a length or two; the winner is likely the horse that has sat second or third and produced the most fluent, length-eating finish rather than a sharp sprint.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Kick Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Get Outta Here or Zarvali seize momentum two furlongs out and the front three draw clear before hold-up horses can close.
scenarios.body: A fast-finishing section to the race sees the leaders quicken into the straight, with the winner already committed and the hold-up brigade left chasing shadows; good-to-firm ground rewards those who have travelled comfortably in the first half.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos Unpicks Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of displaced prominent types — Hambelton and Napolian — push forward and compromise the pace, turning it into a more genuinely contested gallop.
scenarios.body: A busier early order creates more genuine pace, stretching the field and potentially playing into the hands of a hold-up runner who gets a stronger-than-expected gallop to aim at; both Hambelton and Napolian carry style-fit discounts having raced out of role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closer Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough from the outset that the front-runners flatten out in the final furlong and a hold-up horse threads through.
scenarios.body: Only Dream Big or Milford Grange would need a rare honest galop at York over a mile to get involved late, and the redistribution flags on this field's true closers make this the least likely shape to fully materialise; Forest Phoenix's tendency to fade rules it out despite a hold-up position.

watchPoints.text: Zarvali's form record shows 7-from-7 on similar going with a mile win in the book — if Kevin Stott positions cleanly behind the leader, it becomes the most potent prominent threat in the field.

Hambelton and Napolian are both natural prominent racers who may push forward early despite the redistribution flag — watch the first furlong to see whether they attempt to contest the pace and inject more tempo than Luzon Heights intends.

Forest Phoenix carries a finish-fading flag and steps sharply up in trip from 5-6f; any punter drawn to its hold-up position should note it is the riskiest profile in the field for getting home over this mile on good-to-firm ground.

Only Dream Big's apprentice claim (3lb, Warren Fentiman) is worth tracking — two recent wins give it form, but it needs a genuinely strong pace to deliver its hold-up finish and the race shape points to a controlled, not a searching, gallop.

races.name: Azets Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Prince Of The Seas
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer with a solid record at 12f on Good ground (third at this distance in similar conditions), though his recent form shows no win since a mark well above current OR=87; Tudhope and O'Meara firing at 6/47 over 14 days, and he arrives fresh off just 7 days' rest — ground and trip suit, but he must find improvement.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and rated markedly above his official mark on our figures, he is fresh from a run just seven days ago. Winless in his last five starts, but with proven form over today's trip and going, he remains a leading threat if that below-par sequence can be bettered.

runners_data.name: Great Bedwyn
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's six-year-old has placed twice from five runs at 12f on similar ground and handles this trip well; 40 days off is a slight query but he returns to the sort of conditions where he has run his best races, and Joe Leavy takes a 5lb claim to bring the weight down meaningfully.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up in two of his last five starts, this gelding tops our figures by a clear margin. He has form over today's trip and going, with only a 40-day absence since his latest run to note — the one to beat on these figures.

runners_data.name: Frankies Dream
runners_data.note: Steps up sharply from 7-9f to 1m2½f here and historically races as a hold-up type rather than a front-runner — flagged for style fit concerns as a consequence; the uncontested lead is an undeniable gift but whether Jennie Candlish's four-year-old can truly see out the trip from the front on fast ground is the central question.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without a win in his last five starts, with three thirds and a second among them. Race-fit after a run 13 days ago and with form over today's going, he rates around midfield and needs more to trouble the principals.

runners_data.name: Dark Moon Rising
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old hold-up type who has form at 10-12f and placed twice on Tapeta but shows only modest recent form (5th, 12th, 8th) — Kevin Ryan sends him out with just one winner in 39 runners over 14 days, and while the going is fine, the recent profile demands a big step up.
runners_data.comment: A clear second is the standout form line in a six-start sequence without a win, sandwiched among minor-race finishes. Fresh from 28 days off and racing for a yard short of form — one success from 39 runners this fortnight — that stable slump is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Glistening Nights
runners_data.note: Fahey's five-year-old is a natural hold-up horse with a placed record at 10f on Good and Soft — shown in midfield on the map because the field holds more hold-up types than slots available at the rear, so Barry McHugh may find positioning a challenge; the style concern slightly tempers appeal despite good going stats (12/15 sim-going runs with one win, five places).
runners_data.comment: Twice second in his last five starts without getting his head in front, he has form over today's trip and going. Fit from a run 13 days ago, he sits mid-table on our figures and looks the type to make the frame again rather than close that gap to the leaders.

runners_data.name: Beach Point
runners_data.note: William Knight's five-year-old has genuine prominent-racing tendencies and consistent placed form at 10f on Good, but faces competition from several rivals for the same early positions; Hector Crouch rides, and the redistribution to midfield reflects a likely compromise position rather than natural territory.
runners_data.comment: A stack of minor-race finishes without a win in his last five starts leaves plenty to prove. He has form over today's trip and going and holds a fair official mark, but sits toward the bottom on our figures and needs a career-best to feature.

runners_data.name: Kahin
runners_data.note: William Haggas's lightly-raced three-year-old has winning form at 9f on Good (most recent run) and placed at 8f — Cieren Fallon takes the ride on a horse stepping up in trip for the first time, which is the key unknown; the prominent style suits this race shape well if the stamina holds.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and was runner-up before that, form that reads well at face value. He rates markedly behind the leaders on our figures, though, leaving a notable gap to bridge on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Stoneacre Donny
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's consistent three-year-old has placed four times from five runs at 10-12f on Good ground and shapes as an ideal stalker — David Allan knows the horse well, and while the win has proven elusive (0W from 8 sim-going runs), the form is dependable and the race shape flatters a prominent, patient ride.
runners_data.comment: A model of consistency with three thirds and two seconds in his last five starts but yet to win in that sequence. Fit from a run 21 days ago and with form over today's trip and going, he rates prominently on our figures and looks the type to go one better.

runners_data.name: Bearin Up
runners_data.note: The most in-form runner in the race on raw evidence — two wins and several places at 8-10f on Good ground in 2025, and Fentiman rides at a useful weight; a three-year-old with genuine prominence who stays in role here, making it one of the most tractable profiles in the field for this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Twice a winner among her last six starts, this filly boasts solid recent form and has raced over today's trip and going before. Fit after a run 13 days ago, she sits mid-table on our figures and needs more to trouble the principals here.

runners_data.name: Ciao Capo
runners_data.note: A progressive three-year-old (4-1-1-4-1 recent form) whose natural instinct is to race prominently, though the number of forward-going types in this field means Cam Hardie may find it harder than usual to secure that position; the four-race winning sequence at 8-10f is compelling but this is a step into a more competitive race shape context.
runners_data.comment: A three-time winner in his last five starts on paper, though he now rates bottom of this field on our figures, matched by a modest official mark. Fresh from 36 days off, the sharpness since his best efforts has cooled and he faces a tough task back up in company.

races.paceDynamic: Frankies Dream is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 10-runner field over 1m2½f on Good to Firm ground at York, and with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, Paul Mulrennan can dictate terms at a pace entirely of his choosing — this is a genuinely uncontested lead scenario. However, Frankies Dream is racing out of its natural role (a hold-up type by history, flagged STYLE_FIT 0.93) and steps up markedly in trip from 7-9f, which limits confidence in its ability to truly capitalise on a soft lead. Behind the leader, the field is congested with prominent-style runners: Kahin, Stoneacre Donny, and Bearin Up are the legitimate prominent types likely to secure early positions just off the pace, while Beach Point, Ciao Capo, and Glistening Nights — all natural front-runners or prominent racers — have been pushed back to midfield on the map because there is simply more pace in this field than positions available up front; Beach Point and Ciao Capo are most likely to push for position but will face competition doing so. The race shape strongly favours hold-up and prominent types who can settle behind a potentially soft gallop and produce a sustained finish on this flat, galloping track — pure closers with stamina and a late kick are best placed, but prominent horses tracking the early pace without over-committing are also well-positioned.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Soft Lead, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Frankies Dream sets a comfortable, uncontested gallop that compresses the field and sets up a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: Frankies Dream controls proceedings from the front without being seriously tested, but the lack of genuine pressure means the pace is moderate, leaving plenty in the tank for those tracking just behind. Hold-up and prominent types settling in the slipstream enjoy a perfect tow into the straight and produce late surges on the fast ground that the leader cannot repel.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trio Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Kahin, Stoneacre Donny, and Bearin Up push forward aggressively and create a genuine pace contest just behind Frankies Dream.
scenarios.body: The early tempo rises as multiple prominent types compete for the same ground behind the leader, injecting enough pace to stretch the field and reward those who run cleanly through the race. Horses who can sit just off the pace and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs on the Good to Firm going benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely modest and the hold-up horses find clear daylight in the straight to run on.
scenarios.body: Prince Of The Seas and Great Bedwyn, both genuine hold-up types with proven stamina at this distance, get a clean passage and finish powerfully on the fast surface. This shape is only moderately likely because the true hold-up contingent is outnumbered by runners pushed back from prominent roles, diluting the quality of the late challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Leader Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Frankies Dream sets a genuinely slow pace and the field fails to respond in time in the straight.
scenarios.body: With a soft gallop and no one willing to commit until late, Frankies Dream steals enough of a margin to hold on despite its hold-up tendencies — an unlikely outcome given the horse's style profile and trip concerns, but plausible if the field is disorganised.

watchPoints.text: Bearin Up is in strong form (two recent wins at this level, genuine prominent racer in role) and the race shape — uncontested soft pace — perfectly suits a horse who can sit just off the leader and sprint home on fast ground; if Fentiman settles him early, he is the most dangerous profile in the race.

Frankies Dream's ability to see out 1m2½f is the biggest single variable — if it weakens sharply in the final two furlongs having set a slow pace, the race could open up very suddenly for closers in behind; watch for any signs of distress or Mulrennan being forced to commit early.

Kahin is lightly raced and stepping up in trip for the first time — if the Haggas three-year-old handles 1m2½f, the recent winning form and prominent style are a strong fit; the trip question is real but worth tracking early to see if Fallon settles him comfortably.

Beach Point and Ciao Capo are both naturally prominent runners likely to compete for the same early positions — if they push hard against each other just behind Frankies Dream, they could inject enough pace to stretch the field and benefit the hold-up horses finishing late.

Prince Of The Seas arrives just 7 days after his last run and has the clearest stamina profile at 12f on Good ground among the hold-up horses — Tudhope is in form and if the race is run to suit closers, his profile is among the most relevant even if recent form has been below par.

races.name: William Hill Keep Your Raceday Positive Handicap

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Triton
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with a win last time on Good that looks solid form, but York's 5f flat track means he will have ground to make up from off the pace; David Tudhope rides for the in-form David O'Meara yard and will be looking for a clear run through on the stands side.
runners_data.comment: A win near the start of a mixed six-start sequence stands out, though the finishes since have been modest, including a below-par effort last time out. Fit after a run 20 days ago and with form over today's trip and going, he rates prominently on our figures and remains a leading threat if he bounces back.

runners_data.name: Brazen Bolt
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who comes from the rear and whose best Good-ground effort here was a 2nd at 5f; Warren Fentiman claims 3lb which helps offset the age, and 34 days off is acceptable, but he needs pace to aim at and rivals to tire.
runners_data.comment: A clear runner-up in the middle of a mixed five-start sequence is the standout effort without a win to date. Fresh from 34 days off and with form over today's trip and going, he rates highly on our figures, though a yard with no success from 32 runners in a fortnight is the concern.

runners_data.name: Spring Is Sprung
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner and the key pace ingredient; Paul Midgley sends her out quickly and she has recorded four consecutive top-four finishes at 5f on Good or Standard, making her the obvious pace anchor even if the style-fit flag suggests she is not operating at peak in this configuration.
runners_data.comment: A win at the start of this six-start sequence has been followed by a run of frame finishes, most recently a third. Fit after a run 20 days ago and with form over today's trip and going, he tops our figures and rates the one to beat, with that below-par middle spell the only slight blot.

runners_data.name: Ancient State
runners_data.note: Upwardly mobile four-year-old with back-to-back wins on Good ground at 5f and 6f, trained by Adam Kirby who fires at 1/12 over 14 days; headgear noted (t/ce) suggests he is switched on, and 13 days since last run is sharp — this profile fits a race run at a fair pace.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last six starts, including last time out, mark him out as an in-form type on paper. Fit after a run 13 days ago and with form over today's trip and going, he still only rates mid-table on our figures against this stronger crowd.

runners_data.name: Eternal Sunshine
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old has strong Good-ground claims (3W5P in similar conditions) and ran just seven days ago so is clearly in a good routine; Lauren Young's 5lb claim is welcome, though the recent string of 0s before that 2nd on Good needs explaining — form is inconsistent.
runners_data.comment: Three unplaced efforts sit at the start of her recent form, but she has improved sharply since, a runner-up last time her best effort, though still yet to win. Fresh from a run just seven days ago and with form over today's trip and going, she rates competitively on our figures and cannot be dismissed.

runners_data.name: Al Hussar
runners_data.note: Ran 2nd on Good at 5f in his most recent outing and has a win on Good in his recent history; the blinkers are a notable headgear flag and Oliver Stammers takes the ride — a prominent racer who is comfortable in fast conditions and well placed tactically here.
runners_data.comment: A win in the middle of his last six starts, with a runner-up and a third among the earlier form, adds up to a tidy recent profile. Fit after a run 15 days ago and with form over today's trip and going, he rates prominently on our figures and poses a serious threat.

runners_data.name: Counsel
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type who has not won on Good in recent form (sim-going record: 0W1P from 4 runs); Conor Whiteley's 5lb claim helps but 34 days off and a moderate recent string make this a tough ask from the back of the field.
runners_data.comment: A win featured in the middle of a modest five-start sequence, either side of which the finishes have been well held. Fresh from 34 days off and with form over today's trip and going, he sits mid-table on our figures and needs more to feature.

runners_data.name: Emerald Harmony
runners_data.note: David Nolan partners this five-year-old who has been busy (ran 7 days ago) and posted a win and two placings on Good at 5f recently — the record in similar conditions (1W5P) gives genuine each-way claims; races prominently which suits the likely shape here.
runners_data.comment: A win the run before last was followed by a runner-up effort last time out, form that reads well at face value. Fresh from a run just seven days ago and with form over today's trip and going, this mare rates in the middle of our figures and remains open to more improvement.

runners_data.name: Castan
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan picks this up for Bryan Smart after 55 days off, which is the longest absence in the field — hold-up style on a track that rewards handy racing, and recent Good-ground form shows a 1st and a 2nd but that STA form is different; the layoff is the key concern.
runners_data.comment: A win featured three runs back, but the finishes either side have been modest, including an eighth. Fresh from 55 days off and with form over today's trip and going, he rates down this field on our figures and has a lot to find fitness-wise.

runners_data.name: Equity Law
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's sprinter has the best recent winning form in the race (1st and 2nd in last two comparable runs) and David Allan is a capable pilot; despite a strong prominent profile, the redistribution to midfield reflects the crowded early positions — his natural racing style may be compromised by the field size, which the style-fit flag acknowledges.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out to back up a runner-up effort before that, his form clearly on the up. Fit after a run 19 days ago and with form over today's trip and going, he still rates down this field on our figures and faces a step up in company.

runners_data.name: Muker
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse reassigned to midfield on the map because the rear section is oversubscribed in this field; Nigel Tinkler sends him out 8 days after his last run but Muker's Good-going record at York's 5f shows a pattern of mid-field finishes rather than closing wins — difficult to trust from off the pace here.
runners_data.comment: A modest run of finishes without a win leaves him with plenty to prove on form. Fresh from a run just eight days ago and with form over today's trip and going, he still rates well on our figures, though a stable managing just one success from 23 runners is a concern.

runners_data.name: Rotokura Belle
runners_data.note: Three-year-old filly who is a natural hold-up type but repositioned on the map due to the congested rear section; Cam Hardie rides for Ivan Furtado and she has won twice on Good at 5f, though her redistribution means she faces a tactical challenge securing her ideal position — the style-fit discount is warranted.
runners_data.comment: Two wins feature among her last six starts, though sandwiched by finishes well beaten. Fit after a run 13 days ago and with form over today's trip and going, she rates near the bottom of this field on our figures, with a yard short of winners a further concern.

runners_data.name: I'm Dan Dare
runners_data.note: Mark Walford's three-year-old has strong recent form (two wins in last four, including on Good) and is a naturally prominent racer who could not get that slot on the map due to the crowded front section; Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim is a plus, but the inability to race where he wants is a genuine risk at York's competitive 5f.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and again three runs back, with runner-up efforts sprinkled through this sequence too. Fit after a run 15 days ago and with form over today's trip and going, he still rates bottom of this field on our figures despite that pair of wins.

races.paceDynamic: Spring Is Sprung is the one confirmed front-runner here and, on Good to Firm ground at York's straight five, she is likely to bowl along at a sustainable pace without any genuine pressuring rival able to match her early stride for stride. Ancient State, Eternal Sunshine, Al Hussar, and Emerald Harmony will all push for prominent positions just behind, creating a busy, competitive early order but not a truly suicidal gallop — the pace is honest rather than frantic. Several runners tagged as redistributed — Equity Law and I'm Dan Dare, both natural prominent types, and Rotokura Belle and Muker as hold-up horses — are unlikely to secure their preferred positions in a field this competitive for early slots, which adds a layer of positional friction that could compromise their chances. With one uncontested leader setting a fair clip and a pack of prominent types just off the pace, this race shape most favours horses who can race handy from stall to line and sustain their effort on quick ground — genuine prominent-to-lead types with proven Good/Good to Firm form hold the clearest tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent types dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Spring Is Sprung leads at a fair clip and the prominent pack of Ancient State, Eternal Sunshine, and Al Hussar track closely and outfinish the hold-up brigade.
scenarios.body: Spring Is Sprung dictates on comfortable terms, and the horses racing in positions two through five on this flat, straight five furlongs are ideally placed to pounce without needing a gap to open; Good to Firm ground suits quick, continuous galloping rather than a late sprint.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader holds on
scenarios.trigger: If Spring Is Sprung finds a smooth lead and the chasing pack expends energy scrapping for position, leaving her undisturbed at the front.
scenarios.body: With no true pressurer to test her early, Spring Is Sprung could dictate a controlled pace that suits her and draws the sting from rivals who burn energy jostling; York's flat five is genuinely front-runner-friendly in fast conditions when the leader is uncontested.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the prominent pack all tie up inside the final furlong, releasing late finishers.
scenarios.body: Ziggy's Triton and Brazen Bolt have the profile to pick up off a true pace, and if the early scramble for position burns up the prominent types, the rear section could close ground rapidly on this quick surface; however, several of the nominal hold-up runners here are redistributed types not truly suited to coming from off the pace, which limits the probability of this shape delivering.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield surge wins
scenarios.trigger: If positional chaos at the break causes the front and back sections to cancel each other out, leaving a clean run from mid-division decisive.
scenarios.body: Emerald Harmony and Equity Law, despite redistribution complications, have the raw speed and Good-ground form to benefit if a gap opens in the middle of the field; this scenario requires a specific set of circumstances — scrimmaging up front and congestion at the rear — making it the least reliable shape to count on.

watchPoints.text: Watch Spring Is Sprung's early stride — if she secures a clear lead unchallenged in the first furlong, the race is effectively set up for handy types and the hold-up brigade will face a near-impossible task on this flat, fast track.

Ancient State is a serious danger if he breaks cleanly from the stalls; back-to-back wins on Good, sharp trainer stats (1/12 over 14 days), and the headgear combination suggest he is primed — a bad start would be the only thing that stops him competing prominently.

The cluster of prominent types (Equity Law, I'm Dan Dare, Eternal Sunshine, Al Hussar, Emerald Harmony) all wanting to race in positions two through five means an early bump or squeeze is likely — watch for any runner checked in the opening stages as that will effectively end their chance over five furlongs.

Rotokura Belle and Muker are both redistributed hold-up types who may attempt to push forward early against their natural inclinations — if either does, it could force a faster early pace than Spring Is Sprung intends to set, which would alter the entire race shape.

Castan arrives after a 55-day break for Bryan Smart — watch the market move in the final 15 minutes; Smart's 0/8 T14 record suggests this is not a yard firing on all cylinders right now, and the layoff combined with a hold-up style makes him vulnerable if ignored at the weights.

races.name: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Apprentice Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Golden West
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with four top-four finishes from nine runs on Good ground including a placed effort at 1m1f, though this 1m4f trip is at the outer reach of his form profile; Tim Easterby in acceptable 14-day form and Jake Dickson takes off a useful 5lb, but needs a stronger pace than Nightsinwhitesatin is likely to set to deliver his best.|
runners_data.comment: Our pick following an improved second last time, arresting a run of below-par efforts before it, with the speed figure backing up that step forward. Trip and going are both proven and a 16-day turnaround keeps him ticking over, leaving only the modest earlier form as a concern.

runners_data.name: Nightsinwhitesatin
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, able to take up the lead unopposed and control tempo entirely on his own terms; headgear noted, and Edward Bethell's yard is operating at 1-from-30 over the past fortnight which tempers expectations, but the positional advantage in this field shape is significant — 50 days since last run is the main concern.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win but rated the best of these on our figures, with a consistent run of seconds and fourths and nothing worse than fourth in her last five starts. A 50-day absence and a yard successful just once from its last thirty runners are the obvious concerns.

runners_data.name: Secret Beach
runners_data.note: Recent form reads poorly (9th, 7th) but won over 1m4f on Good ground earlier in the season; Donald McCain's small yard has a 1-from-10 recent strike rate and Warren Fentiman is unclaimed, while this track and trip profile look genuine — the inconsistency is the red flag here.|
runners_data.comment: A win earlier in the campaign and a second deeper in the form show a ceiling, but the finishes have tailed off since (9th, 5th, 7th last time). Proven over today's trip and going, a 16-day turnaround keeps him fresh, though our 82 rating puts him only modestly above his mark and mid-pack here.

runners_data.name: High Fibre
runners_data.note: An interesting runner returning from a 645-day absence (51 jumps runs intervening), previously winning over 2m on Good ground which marks him out as the field's most credible stayer; Harry Fry's yard is in sharp form at 3-from-4 over 14 days, and Mason Paetel's claim could be significant if fitness is intact after the long layoff.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last four starts but rated the second-best of these on our figures, well clear of his official mark, despite finishes that read sixth, unplaced, eighth and seventh. Trip and going are both proven, leaving the untapped potential in those figures as the case for him.

runners_data.name: Humble Spark
runners_data.note: Consistent place-getter who has finished second four times in his last five Good-ground runs including over 1m3f-1m5f, making the trip look ideal; Jim Goldie's yard is active at 7-from-44 and Lauren Young claims 3lb, but the absence of a win from those placed efforts raises questions about whether he can convert.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last six starts but with three seconds among those finishes and nothing worse than a ninth, the underlying form is solid. Trip and going are both proven, and a 20-day turnaround keeps him ticking over into this at a workmanlike level.

runners_data.name: Nicator
runners_data.note: Progressive four-year-old with four placed efforts from five runs on Good or Good to Firm, operating over shorter trips (8f-10f) and stepping up significantly to 1m4f here for the first time; Taryn Langley claims 3lb and Kevin Philippart De Foy has a single winner from 17 recent runners — the trip extension is the critical unknown.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five but placed repeatedly, with three seconds among those finishes and only one poor run to note. Today's going is proven, though our 77 rating matches his official mark and leaves him 8th of 10 — consistent but needing to find a bit more.

runners_data.name: Optician
runners_data.note: Won over 1m4f on Soft ground and is a genuine hold-up type by nature, but with multiple hold-up horses in this field he is likely to find himself racing in midfield against his instincts rather than from his preferred deep position; Michael Herrington's yard is in reasonable form at 3-from-18, and the step back to Good from Soft is not an automatic concern given his one turf win came on Soft.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, snapping a run that included a pulled-up effort and two unplaced runs, and the figures still edge him above his official mark. Trip and going are both proven, with a 26-day turnaround giving him a chance to build on that success.

runners_data.name: Green Sky
runners_data.note: Won over 1m4f on Good ground, so the trip and conditions look fine on paper, and Rod Millman's runner is freshened up on just seven days rest; as a true hold-up type he is likely to find midfield where he cannot fully execute his race, and the yard is winless from 21 runners over the past fortnight, which adds to the caution here.|
runners_data.comment: Won last time out on a swift 7-day turnaround, though fourth and eighth before that were below-par. Trip and going are both proven and the figures edge her above her official mark, but a yard yet to land a success from its last twenty-one runners is a concern.

runners_data.name: Pleasant Man
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran who won over 1m4f on Good ground and has three thirds at this distance, making him course-appropriate; Joey Ramsden's yard has a recent winner and Alex Jary is unclaimed, but the age and the moderate OR of 70 suggest he needs things to go his way positionally — his prominent style suits the likely race shape well.|
runners_data.comment: A consistent sort with three thirds and a win among his last six starts, but rated close to the bottom of this field on our figures and only a shade above his official mark. Trip and going are both proven, and a rapid 8-day turnaround at least keeps him fresh.

runners_data.name: Queen Roslyn
runners_data.note: Won over 2m1f on Soft and has placed form at marathon trips, so stamina is not in doubt, but this OR drop to 62 reflects a sharp recent decline including an 11th on Good ground; a true hold-up operator who will be shuffled into midfield by the volume of similar types in this race, and her best form has come on Soft or Soft-Heavy which makes the Good to Firm description here a genuine concern.|
runners_data.comment: Two wins in her last five starts are the highlight, though the form has cooled since, unplaced last time. Trip and going are both proven, but a yard managing only one success from its last twenty is a further concern.

races.paceDynamic: Nightsinwhitesatin is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should settle into a comfortable, uncontested rhythm over this 1m4f trip on Good to Firm ground at York — a surface that rewards horses who can travel economically and sustain their effort rather than those hunting a late gap. Nicator, High Fibre, and Pleasant Man will press into prominent positions just off the pace, creating an orderly moving gallop rather than a searching one, which historically at York over this trip flatters those who can sit close to the tempo without expending energy. The hold-up brigade — Golden West, Humble Spark, Secret Beach, and the genuinely rearward types Optician, Green Sky, and Queen Roslyn — will be hunting a pace injection that is unlikely to arrive, and with the field containing more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate, Optician, Green Sky, and Queen Roslyn are most likely to be shuffled into midfield against their natural instincts, further diluting their finishing prospects. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel just off Nightsinwhitesatin's uncontested lead and pick up smoothly in the straight, rather than deep closers who need a truly honest pace to generate the gaps they require.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nightsinwhitesatin Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Nightsinwhitesatin dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent riders travel comfortably throughout.
scenarios.body: Nightsinwhitesatin sets a sustainable tempo on Good to Firm, and horses sitting just off the pace — Nicator and Pleasant Man — find the tempo perfectly calibrated to their strengths, picking off the leader in the final two furlongs without requiring a searching finish. This shape is the most likely outcome given sole front-runner status and the track's tendency to reward prominent, economical travel over 1m4f.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Runners Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If Nightsinwhitesatin sets a genuinely slow tempo that compresses the field and triggers a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A slow pace bunches the runners entering the straight and negates the positional advantage of the prominent horses, allowing genuine hold-up types Golden West and Humble Spark to thread through late as the field idles in front. However, Good to Firm ground at York tends to produce strong-travelling prominent winners over this trip rather than late swoops, limiting the probability of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Even Pace, Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If Nightsinwhitesatin is allowed to stride on and sets a more honest gallop that gradually stretches the field.
scenarios.body: A stronger early tempo turns this into a genuine stamina contest over the final three furlongs, suiting High Fibre — whose profile includes wins at 2m — and Humble Spark, who has placed repeatedly over 1m4f-plus on Good ground. The prominent horses who lack resolution may fade, handing the advantage to stayers who have been underestimated in the pace map.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Hold-Up Types Misfire
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems at a compact York straight cause the redistributed midfield types to find no room late.
scenarios.body: Optician, Green Sky, and Queen Roslyn — already racing out of their natural hold-up role and squeezed into midfield — encounter trouble in the straight and fail to produce their finishing effort when it matters, handing the race to whichever prominent horse travels best. This scenario is the least likely given the clear, wide York straight, but the sheer volume of horses in atypical positions elevates the risk slightly.

watchPoints.text: Nightsinwhitesatin's uncontested lead means the entire race tempo is in Cian Horgan's hands — if he allows a slow early gallop the race compresses dangerously, but if he dictates a controlled rhythm from the front his positional advantage is enormous and the horse cannot easily be attacked.

High Fibre's 645-day absence after 51 jumps runs is an extraordinary data point — Harry Fry's 3-from-4 recent stable form suggests the yard is confident, but a horse this far removed from turf flat racing could either run a career-best or be completely unprepared.

Nicator is stepping up by at least 4f on any previous run in his form history — if the trip extension proves too much he will drop away tamely from a prominent position and potentially interfere with runners behind him in the straight.

Optician, Green Sky, and Queen Roslyn are all genuine hold-up types racing out of their natural position due to field composition — watch for all three to find midfield traffic rather than the clear daylight they need, which could affect betting markets if they are backed on the strength of past running style.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this race despite the card showing Good — York's straight 1m4f track on quick ground typically suits prominent, economical travellers and can expose hold-up horses who need a strongly-run contest to generate momentum.
